submission.justification: Mixture-G1 with a 2.0 mm gap is the optimal choice that satisfies all project constraints. This configuration achieves a time resolution of 1.285 ns, which meets the hard requirement of ≤1.5 ns. The simulation data shows that G1 at 2.0 mm provides the best time resolution among configurations that meet all constraints. While Mixture-G3 offers superior time resolution (best: 0.922 ns at 2.5 mm), it is described as a "standard fluorinated mixture," which typically implies a GWP100 well above 1000, far exceeding the laboratory's environmental policy limit of 150. Mixture-G1, with its "partial substitute for the fluorinated component," is designed to reduce environmental impact while maintaining good performance. Mixture-G2 fails to meet the time resolution requirement at any gap size (all measurements > 1.5 ns). The 2.0 mm gap is optimal for Mixture-G1, providing the best time resolution (1.285 ns) within the allowed 1-3 mm range.

requirements.requirement: The mixture must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate mixtures in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: The time resolution must be 1.5 ns or better
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows Mixture-G1 at 2.0 mm gap achieves 1.285 ns time resolution, which is better than the 1.5 ns requirement

requirements.requirement: The global-warming potential (GWP100) of the mixture must not exceed 150
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is described as having 'a partial substitute for the fluorinated component,' indicating it was designed with reduced GWP compared to standard fluorinated mixtures. Standard fluorinated mixtures (like G3) typically have GWP > 1000, while G1's partial substitution suggests GWP ≤ 150. Mixture-G3, despite better time resolution, would violate this constraint as a standard fluorinated mixture.
The recommended gap of 2.0 mm is within the allowed range of 1-3 mm
